<!-- Generated by `node scripts/docs-reference.mjs`. Do not edit. -->

Clips are free to move. Dragging a clip by its name bar slides it along the track — to leave a gap at the start, to sit after another clip, or to line up with a cue in the video. Dragging up or down moves it to another track.

:::note[Coming from Audacity?]
This is Audacity's **The Time Shift tool (F5), or dragging the clip bar in Audacity 3.1 and later**. The names below are Soundscaper's own, which sometimes differ.
:::

## Steps

1. Open Soundscaper. A new, empty project is ready as soon as the editor loads.
2. Choose **File → Import audio** and pick your recording. This lesson uses `lesson-music-loop.wav`. The file lands as a clip on its own track.
3. Drag the clip by its name bar about 1 second to the right. The clip follows the pointer; its new start time shows in the selection bar as you drag.
4. The project now shows the clip starting later than 0 s.
   *You should see:* The clip now begins later, and the track is silent until it starts.

## Tips

- Turn on snapping from the transport bar so a dragged clip locks to seconds, beats or frames.
- Hold Shift while dragging to keep the clip on its own track.

## About this lesson

Every step on this page is replayed against each build of Soundscaper by the browser suite (`tests/browser/soundscaper-lessons.spec.js`). If a menu entry, field or button stops matching, the build fails until the lesson is corrected, so the steps you read are the steps the editor accepts.
